features.description: Worktree binding registry module: install-level storage of per-plan worktree bindings at $DONTPANIC_HOME/worktrees.json, mirroring the projects.json registry pattern.
features.acceptance: a new worktrees registry module stores bindings at $DONTPANIC_HOME/worktrees.json honoring the same DONTPANIC_HOME / JARVIS_HOME resolution as projects.json, with Pydantic extra=forbid; an invalid/corrupt registry file degrades to empty-plus-warn ONLY for read-only consumers (the worktree-status model and its renderers, which must surface a registry-corrupt warning instead of silently rendering nothing), while the module also exposes a strict load that RAISES on a corrupt file for the plan-mutating guard path; a binding record carries plan_id, repo_root, worktree_path, branch, base_ref (the ref name the base was resolved FROM), base_sha (the resolved commit SHA, pinned at create time and never recomputed), owner_actor (DONTPANIC_ACTOR env else user@host), created_at; the module exposes pure add/get/remove/list operations that refuse a second binding for an already-bound plan and refuse a worktree_path already claimed by another binding; tests cover round-trip persistence, double-bind refusal, path-collision refusal, invalid-file degradation, and home-resolution precedence, all against a temp home with no network.

features.description: Gate-time binding capture: plan lock / audit / close AND the orchestrate dispatch (build) path record the worktree binding snapshot into the plan's audit evidence when a binding exists.
features.acceptance: when a binding exists for the plan, `plan lock`, `plan audit`, `plan close`, and the orchestrate dispatch entry point (the build path) write a binding snapshot (worktree_path, base_ref, base_sha, branch, owner_actor, captured_at) into the plan's audit evidence alongside the gate artifacts they already produce; when no binding exists the commands behave exactly as today and write no snapshot (additive, proven by a no-binding regression test); fixture tests run a gate command and a dispatch entry inside a bound temp worktree and assert the snapshot lands with the recorded values.

features.description: Wrong-worktree refusal: every plan-mutating entry point (lock, audit, close, disposition, orchestrate dispatch) refuses from a working tree other than the plan's bound worktree unless explicitly overridden, and the override is recorded.
features.acceptance: `plan lock`, `plan audit`, `plan close`, `plan disposition`, and the orchestrate dispatch entry point resolve the invoking working tree (git rev-parse --show-toplevel) and, for a bound plan, refuse BEFORE any gate side effect or evidence write when the invoking tree differs from the bound worktree_path OR when the invoking directory is not inside any git worktree at all (not-in-a-worktree is still not the bound worktree), OR when the bound worktree's CURRENT branch differs from the recorded branch (branch drift / detached HEAD must not let a correct path mutate a wrong branch) with a message naming both the invoking tree and the bound worktree_path plus the exact create/override commands; an explicit override flag with a required reason proceeds and records the override (plan_id, invoking path, bound path, reason, actor, timestamp) into the plan's audit evidence; plans with no binding in a VALID (or absent) registry are never refused (backward-compatibility regression test); a registry file that EXISTS but is corrupt/unparseable FAILS CLOSED — every guarded entry point refuses with a distinct registry-corrupt error naming the file, never the unbound passthrough (a corrupt worktrees.json must not silently disable wrong-worktree protection; fixture test with a garbage registry); DontPanic has NO merge command — merging is the operator's external gh ritual, so the guarded set above IS the complete plan-mutating surface, and this feature OWNS that guard with a CLI-surface test asserting the plan command namespace exposes no merge subcommand; tests cover refusal per guarded entry point, override-with-reason recording, and the unbound passthrough.

features.description: Worktree-status model + `dontpanic plan worktree list`: one pure model over registry + git state, rendered by the list command.
features.acceptance: a single pure function builds the worktree-status model from the registry plus per-worktree git state — per binding: plan_id, recorded branch, current_branch (the worktree's actual checked-out branch, with drift between them rendered as broken/drifted, never hidden), worktree_path, owner_actor, dirty (true iff the worktree's porcelain-format status output (git_status_porcelain) is non-empty), untracked_count (PINNED: the number of untracked entries exactly as porcelain status reports them in its default untracked-files mode — a collapsed untracked directory counts as ONE entry; a fixture with an untracked directory containing multiple files asserts this), and a broken flag when the recorded worktree_path no longer exists, is not a git worktree, or is not a worktree OF the recorded repo_root (verified against repo_root's own worktree list / common git dir — an arbitrary unrelated git repository at that path is broken, not healthy); broken bindings are RENDERED, never silently dropped; when the registry file is corrupt the model carries a registry_corrupt warning flag instead of silently rendering an empty list; `dontpanic plan worktree list` prints one row per binding from this model; tests cover clean, dirty, untracked-only, and broken-binding states through the model and the list renderer on temp git repos.

features.description: Explicit, audited, safe cleanup: remove a plan worktree only when clean; no force path in v0; close never auto-removes.
features.acceptance: `dontpanic plan worktree remove <plan-id>` refuses when the bound worktree has ANY modified, staged, or untracked files (printing the offending paths) AND refuses every unhealthy binding outright — missing path, path that is not a git worktree, a worktree not belonging to the recorded repo_root, detached HEAD, or current branch differing from the recorded branch — naming the specific failed health check (only a healthy, clean, bound worktree on its recorded branch is ever removed), and removes the worktree (git worktree remove without --force) plus the registry binding only when fully clean; every removal appends an audit entry (plan_id, worktree_path, branch, owner_actor, removed_by — the actor performing the cleanup, resolved the same way as owner_actor and recorded even when it differs — and removed_at) to a worktree audit log under $DONTPANIC_HOME; no command in this plan deletes a dirty worktree or exposes a force-removal flag (asserted by a CLI-surface test); `plan close` performs NO worktree removal — at most it prints the explicit remove command (regression test on the close path); tests cover clean removal with audit entry, dirty refusal listing files, untracked-only refusal, and the close-does-not-remove guarantee. the remove command loads the registry via the STRICT path and refuses on a corrupt registry file before touching any filesystem state (fail closed).

features.description: `dontpanic plan worktree create <plan-id>`: create the per-plan git worktree from an explicit recorded base and bind it in the registry.
features.acceptance: `dontpanic plan worktree create <plan-id>` resolves the plan dir and derives repo_root AUTHORITATIVELY from the plan dir's containing repository (rev-parse show-toplevel of the resolved plan directory) — every git invocation the command makes runs against that repo_root, never the invoking checkout's repository (proven by a test invoking create from an unrelated git repo); it creates a git worktree (git_worktree_add) at the deterministic path $DONTPANIC_HOME/worktrees/<repo-dir-name>/<plan-id> (outside the main working tree) on the branch plan/<plan-id> (plan ids are already filesystem/ref-safe slugs; the derivation is identity plus the pinned prefixes, asserted by test); a pre-existing branch of that name refuses in v0 (no reuse, no force); the base is NEVER the invoking checkout's HEAD implicitly: by default it is repo_root's default branch resolved by a PINNED rule: origin's HEAD symbolic ref when an origin exists and origin/HEAD resolves; when origin exists but origin/HEAD does not resolve, fall back to the local rule; the local rule prefers main and falls back to master, and if BOTH exist main wins deterministically; if none of these resolve the command refuses naming the rule and an explicit base_flag (a base-ref CLI option) may select a different base; in every case the base is resolved via rev-parse to base_sha, both base_ref and base_sha are printed in the command output and recorded verbatim in the binding, and the worktree is created AT base_sha so the recorded SHA cannot drift from what was checked out; an unresolvable base refuses before any worktree is created; on success the registry holds the full binding and the command prints worktree_path, branch, base_ref, base_sha, and owner_actor; an already-bound plan refuses naming the existing binding; an occupied target path refuses without touching it; a failed git invocation leaves NO registry entry behind (no half-bind); tests cover default-base resolution (asserting it tracks the default branch, not the invoking HEAD on a divergent checkout), explicit base_flag recording, unresolvable-base refusal, pre-existing-branch refusal, wrong-invoking-repo independence, create, double-bind refusal, occupied-path refusal, and git-failure rollback on temp git repos with no network. the create command loads the registry via the STRICT path and refuses on a corrupt registry file before creating any worktree or branch (fail closed — it mutates the registry, so it never proceeds on one it cannot parse).

features.description: Operator brief + dashboard visibility: the worktree-status model rendered in the operator brief and the dashboard state payload.
features.acceptance: the operator brief includes an active-worktrees section driven by the SAME worktree-status model as the list command (branch, dirty, untracked_count, owner_actor, broken bindings included); the REAL dashboard state producer (the dashboard build path that writes the on-disk JSON state the shell loads) is wired to include the active-worktrees block — a producer test runs the real build path against a temp registry and asserts the block lands in the written state file and passes the existing no-secret-shapes guard; the dashboard UI ACTUALLY RENDERS the block: a DOM-level integration test loads the real dashboard page module with a payload fixture and asserts the rendered surface shows branch, dirty state, untracked count, actor, and broken bindings for the fixture entries, plus an honest empty state when no bindings exist (nothing fabricated); tests cover the brief section, the payload block, and the DOM render for clean, dirty, and broken-binding fixtures, and assert model parity between the three renderers (list, brief, dashboard).
